item.title: Zelda: Ocarina of Time Is Actually the Perfect Way to Introduce Kids to Nintendo
item.dc:creator: Rebecca Corgan
item.category: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time
item.description: Parents are debating whether the Ocarina of Time remake is too scary for kids. Here’s the case for the child-era half as a first Nintendo game.
item.content:encoded: Walk into The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time’s Kokiri Forest, and it feels like you’re walking into a picture book. Especially in the remake, everything is moss-green and dappled with light. Fairies flit about. Kokiri children are rhythmically attending to their tasks. Everyone is friendly, everything is beautiful, and the world both feels safe and makes sense. Then you walk into the Great Deku Tree and spiders start falling from the ceiling. My daughter screamed. I jumped, too, and I knew they were coming.

item.title: Magic Is Bringing Back Its Most Controversial Creature Type
item.dc:creator: Tomas Franzese
item.description: Magic: The Gathering's Aaron Forsythe tells Polygon he knows when more Sliver cards will come to the game
item.content:encoded: Whether you love or hate Sliver decks in Magic: The Gathering, you should prepare for more Sliver cards to make their way to the game soon. Vice President of Design Aaron Forsythe revealed as much during an in-person interview with Polygon at MagicCon: Atlanta 2026.

item.title: Blade Runner Is Officially Getting The AAA Game Treatment
item.dc:creator: Tomas Franzese
item.description: Alcon Entertainment confirmed it has had discussions about creating a AAA game based on Blade Runner
item.content:encoded: Alcon Entertainment, which owns the Blade Runner franchise, confirmed in a recent interview that it has discussed making a AAA game based on the beloved sci-fi series. It's an exciting development for Blade Runner, which has never quite found its footing in gaming despite how influential its visual style and narrative themes have been.

item.title: The Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake Is an Event Even if You’re Not Playing It
item.dc:creator: Oli Welsh
item.category: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time
item.description: Watching personal reactions to Nintendo's Switch 2 version of The Legend of Zelda: OoT is beautiful
item.content:encoded: Switchboard is Polygon's weekly newsletter for all things Nintendo, sent on Thursdays and published on the site on Saturdays. You can subscribe here.

item.title: 8 Iconic Video Game Villains Who Were Actually Right the Whole Time
item.dc:creator: Rebecca Corgan
item.description: The best video game villains of all time had motives that, when you think about them, actually made a whole lot of sense.
item.content:encoded: Grab your gavel: Court is in session for eight of gaming’s most misunderstood villains. Their charges? One occupied planet, one erased painting, one underwater utopia gone to rot, and a truly staggering body count. But, all that aside, what if these bad guys were actually making a somewhat decent point? Read between the lines of their melodramatic monologues, and perhaps you’ll realize that, say, a centuries-long guilt trip over one catastrophic mistake was in fact understandable rationale for wanting to tear the world down and start over. Or not: You get to decide. Just read each villain’s case file below before reaching a verdict — you might not love where the evidence actually points.

item.title: Ubisoft Is Reportedly Bringing A Beloved Series Back After Nearly Two Decades
item.dc:creator: Tomas Franzese
item.description: A new Rainbow Six: Vegas game is in the works at Ubisoft Montreal, according to a new report
item.content:encoded: Before Rainbow Six Siege, Ubisoft published two Rainbow Six: Vegas games for PS3 and Xbox 360. Now, a new report suggests that a third Rainbow Six: Vegas game is in the works, moving the franchise beyond Siege.

item.title: Magic: The Gathering’s 5 Best and Weirdest Star Trek References
item.dc:creator: Sam Nelson
item.description: The set has nods to some of the franchise’s silliest moments
item.content:encoded: Magic: The Gathering’s Star Trek is a love letter to the franchise. The set uses sagas to pay tribute to standout episodes like “The Inner Light” and “In the Pale Moonlight,” and it’s stuffed with cards representing legendary characters and spacecraft along with famous quotes like “Live long and prosper.” But the set also features plenty of deeper cuts, embracing the times that Star Trek was silly, controversial, and downright terrible. These are the five best references to the franchise’s worst and weirdest moments.

item.title: Big Walk's AI Controversy Overshadows a Remarkable Creative Achievement
item.dc:creator: Matt Patches
item.description: House House's 2026 Game of the Year contender used an LLM to get over the finish line, but the run to get there was pure human craft.
item.content:encoded: And then we took Kalonica [Quigley] in, who's now the fifth member of House House, and gave her a tour of this island. It was much smaller than the final thing, but it was really just an island with a bunch of trees and a few rocks, and maybe the red lookout tower was there, or an earlier version of it. There was a giant floating sphere and maybe just some really primitive shapes. But we took her around and had this really amazing experience just exploring together. It felt social and fun, like hanging out with your friends.

item.title: The McElroys take sibling rivalry to a new level | Shelf Quest
item.dc:creator: Matt Patches
item.description: Return of the best boys! Griffin and Justin McElroy take to the shelves at videogamesnewyork to pull out some of the deepest video game cuts we've seen so far! From NES classics like Shadowgate to modern favorites like Persona 4 Golden and everything between, the podcasting brothers have a nose for the hits. Watch to find out the truth about David Cage's Heavy Rain, why the Kinect might be the best console ever, and what happened to Griffin's gold Ocarina of Time cartridge... it's Shelf Quest!

item.title: Every GTA 6 Actor Rumored and Confirmed by Rockstar Ahead of Launch
item.dc:creator: Jen Glennon
item.description: Who will play Jason, Lucia, and other major characters in GTA 6? Rockstar hasn't made an official reveal yet, but the internet has plenty of ideas.
item.content:encoded: It's been an excruciatingly long wait, but we're just days away from the launch of Grand Theft Auto 6. Ahead of the game's launch for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X, Rockstar Games has yet to reveal any official details about the actors who will appear in GTA 6, including the central couple, Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos.

item.title: Zelda Fans Who Loved Ocarina of Time Need to Play This Game Next
item.dc:creator: Jason Venter
item.category: The Legend of Zelda: A Link to the Past
The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time
item.description: Ocarina of Time features some memorable moments, and many of them were similarly compelling in a previous Zelda adventure.
item.content:encoded: By now, you’ve probably had time to play The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake on the Nintendo Switch 2. You’ve marveled at what a great job it does of bringing the classic Nintendo 64 adventure to a new generation, with visual improvements and quality-of-life changes to make it more palatable for that new audience. Maybe you’ve even run through it a second time.

item.title: 20 Years Later, A Classic Nintendo DS Puzzle Game Officially Returns
item.dc:creator: Willa Rowe
item.description: Level-5 is remaking the classic Nintendo DS puzzle game Professor Layton and the Curious Village and it's due out in 2027
item.content:encoded: Next year will mark the 20th anniversary of Level-5's beloved Professor Layton series. To celebrate, the company has announced it is remaking Professor Layton and the Curious Village.

item.title: Fallout 5 and Fallout Remasters Officially Announced
item.dc:creator: Michael McWhertor
item.description: Bethesda Softworks updates fans on the future of Fallout, which includes new Fallout 3 and New Vegas releases and Fallout 5.
item.content:encoded: Xbox wants more Fallout, and after a yearslong drought of new games, Bethesda Softworks is making it happen. Bethesda plans to release remasters of both Fallout 3 and Fallout: New Vegas for modern platforms, the company said in July in a massive roadmap of the developer's future. Those remasters are part of a larger plan to reinvest in Fallout games — including Fallout 5, which is currently in pre-production — and a new untitled project at Obsidian Entertainment.

item.title: Blizzard Officially Responds to Disappointed Overwatch Fans Over Hero 55
item.dc:creator: Michael McWhertor
item.description: Overwatch's next hero, Hudson, will be a Damage (DPS) character, not a support. Fans are disappointed by the switch and Blizzard is responding.
item.content:encoded: Blizzard Entertainment is about to make good on the promise of delivering 10 new heroes to Overwatch in 2026, with the final addition arriving in December. The 10th new hero coming to Overwatch in 2026 is an Omnic detective named Hudson, and he'll arrive alongside the launch of season 6. Hudson was officially revealed on Thursday, but many Overwatch fans aren't pleased with a key aspect of his character.

item.title: 6 Most-Anticipated Steam Games You Should Add to Your Wishlist Right Now
item.dc:creator: Giovanni Colantonio
item.description: The best upcoming Steam games to add to your Wishlist include an open-world RPG, a narrative adventure, and... a game about slaps?
item.content:encoded: Sometimes when we put together a new installment of Wishlister, Polygon’s weekly newsletter that highlights upcoming Steam games, we look to events like Steam Next Fest and the Triple-I Initiative to dig up gems. But the most tried-and-true method we’ve found for finding promising games is simply stumbling into them by accident.

item.title: Cities: Skylines' Best Replacement Is Finally Here and Better than Expected
item.dc:creator: Josh Broadwell
item.description: Transport Fever 3 turned me into a lover of logistics-based city builder games with how much more hands-on it is compared to Cities: Skylines
item.content:encoded: 2026 is the year I got massively into city builders, and by massively I mean I played Cities: Skylines more than anything else for the first half of the year. I started dabbling with city builder-slash-logistics games in the second half of the year, like Anno 117, and turned my attention to Transport Fever 3 soon after. When I first learned about Transport Fever 3, I called it "like" Cities: Skylines. It looked a lot like a traditional city builder, albeit one where you focus on roads more than zoning. After playing it over the last month or so, though, I realize the difference between city builder and logistics planner is a lot more distinct than I initially gave it credit for — and I've irreversibly become a logistics sicko.

item.title: 8 New TV Shows to Watch This Weekend on Netflix, Prime Video, and HBO (November 13-15)
item.dc:creator: Maria Loreto
item.category: The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power
item.description: On this week's TV column, there's the return of one of the biggest fantasy franchises in the world, a new Netflix horror, and more.
item.content:encoded: It’s a big weekend for new TV. VisionQuesthas concluded its first season, including a post-credits scene with big implications for Avengers: Doomsday. The Lord of the Rings: Rings of Power is back with a third season, continuing the story of a Middle-earth set thousands of years before Bilbo and Frodo Baggins. The Body is also available on Netflix, delivering a fun and campy high school drama with some religious horror thrown in the mix.

item.title: Blood of Dawnwalker Finally Gets Its Most Requested Feature Next Week
item.dc:creator: Willa Rowe
item.description: Blood of Dawnwalker update 1.2 will add New Game + next week after overwhelming fan demand
item.content:encoded: It's been just over two months since The Blood of Dawnwalker was released and fans have been clamoring for one missing feature for basically that long. Now developer Rebel Wolves is set to appease that demand with the upcoming update 1.2. Yes, New Game Plus is going to be a reality for the vampire RPG.

item.title: The Game Awards 2026 Nominees Announcement Confirmed for Nov. 17
item.dc:creator: Michael McWhertor
item.description: Geoff Keighley's The Game Awards will announce 2026's nominees, including Game of the Year, on Tuesday, Nov. 17.
item.content:encoded: The Game Awards 2026 is approaching, and this year's award nominees are set to be announced on Tuesday, Nov. 17. That's according to host and creator of The Game Awards Geoff Keighley, who announced Friday that 2026's nominees will be revealed during a livestream — that just happens to be coming two days ahead of the year's most anticipated game, Grand Theft Auto 6.

item.title: Every Free Game You Can Keep on Steam, Epic, PlayStation Plus, and Xbox (Nov. 13-19)
item.dc:creator: Ashely Claudino
item.description: Epic Games Store, Steam, and Xbox have some free games to keep you busy before GTA 6 drops.
item.content:encoded: Next week the world will stop for many players with the launch of Grand Theft Auto 6. If you've already preloaded GTA 6, then you'll be ready to hit "Play" as soon as it becomes available on Nov. 19. In the meantime, you have to find a game that'll keep you busy.

item.title: Magic Just Revealed 19 New Cards From 2027’s First Set — Including a $30 Reprint With Stunning Art
item.dc:creator: Corey Plante
item.description: Wizards of the Coast gave Nauctis: The Sunken Realm a proper introduction at MagicCon: Atlanta.
item.content:encoded: Magic: The Gathering is heading underwater, and we’ve just gotten a closer look at what’s lurking in the depths of a new plane called Nauctis. During Friday’s preview panel at MagicCon: Atlanta, Wizards of the Coast revealed 19 cards from Nauctis: The Sunken Realm (including different art variants), the upcoming set that introduces an ocean plane to Magic’s Multiverse. Launching on Feb. 5, 2027, the set trades typical fantasy settings like Dominaria or Ikoria for sprawling underwater cities and aquatic creatures, with greater dangers waiting farther below the surface.

item.title: The 25 Best Switch 2 Games
item.dc:creator: Oli Welsh
item.description: The best Nintendo Switch 2 games include Zelda: Ocarina of Time, Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave, and plenty more.
item.content:encoded: That's in addition to stellar third-party support, with almost unanimous buy-in from indies and several big publishers going all-in on porting their biggest titles to Switch 2 — notably Square Enix, with the Final Fantasy 7 series, and Capcom, with Resident Evil, Onimusha, Pragmata, and more coming.

item.title: Steam’s Angriest New Game Is the Perfect Place to Channel Your AI Hate
item.dc:creator: Giovanni Colantonio
item.description: Virtue and a Sledgehammer is a rage-filled takedown of AI, but it's more interested in what makes us human.
item.content:encoded: The greater threat of an unchecked AI industry is that it will siphon the soul out of humanity. And what are we without that?

item.title: Xbox Shares New Fable Trailer that Divides the Fanbase
item.dc:creator: Francesco Cacciatore
item.description: Xbox shared a new gameplay trailer for the upcoming Fable reboot, and the bleak footage divided fans.
item.content:encoded: On Nov. 12, Xbox CEO Asha Sharma shared a new gameplay trailer for Fable, the long-anticipated fourth installment in the Fable series, developed by Playground Games. While excitement for the game remains high, many fans shared their negative reactions online, confirming that this will be another controversial release.

item.title: New Game from Doom studio and New Wolfenstein Announced
item.dc:creator: Ashely Claudino
item.description: Xbox CEO Asha Sharma has unveiled upcoming Bethesda games coming from the studios that made Doom and Wolfenstein.
item.content:encoded: Xbox is celebrating its 25th anniversary this month, and it's been spoiling fans left and right. Xbox games like Minecraft, Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024, Gears E-Day, and more received celebratory freebies. Beyond the awesome free in-game items, players were lucky enough to get a few exciting announcements coming from Bethesda-owned studios, Id Software and MachineGames.

item.title: Leaked Dune Magic Secret Lair Has Amazing Value Reprints and 9 New Cards
item.dc:creator: Francesco Cacciatore
item.description: An unconfirmed Dune x Magic Secret Lair superdrop leaked, and it includes great reprints and 9 new cards.
item.content:encoded: One popular sci-fi property is the talk of the Magic: The Gathering community right now, and it's not Star Trek. On Nov. 12, leaks started to emerge online about a Dune Secret Lair drop, and while still unconfirmed, this new Universes Beyond collaboration seems legitimate.

item.title: 8 Near-Perfect Xbox 360 Games That Are Forgotten Masterpieces
item.dc:creator: Randy Rhodes
item.description: From Viva Piñata to The Saboteur, these forgotten Xbox 360 masterpieces deserve another shot today.
item.content:encoded: The Xbox 360 era was a marvelous generation and the last time publishers regularly bet on strange, original ideas. Plenty of those bets paid off, from Gears of War to Assassin's Creed. But time hasn't been kind to all of them, and some of the generation's best games have been out of the conversation so long that a whole new wave of players has never heard of them.

item.title: The 25 Best Nintendo Switch 2 Games in 2026
item.dc:creator: Oli Welsh
item.description: What are the best Nintendo Switch 2 games? From Zelda: Ocarina of Time to Mario Kart World, here are our favorites
item.content:encoded: That's in addition to stellar third-party support, with almost unanimous buy-in from indies and several big publishers going all-in on porting their biggest titles to Switch 2 — notably Square Enix, with the Final Fantasy 7 series, and Capcom, with Resident Evil, Onimusha, Pragmata, and more coming.

item.title: Steam Makes Popular World War II Strategy Game Free to Play This Weekend
item.dc:creator: Sam Hill
item.description: Steam players can try Company of Heroes 3 for free this weekend before picking up the World War II strategy game at a discount.
item.content:encoded: Steam regularly gives PC players an opportunity to try something new without spending a cent and these promotions are particularly useful for strategy fans, as they offer a chance to test out a new experience before deciding whether it's worth the investment.

item.title: Xbox CEO Hints Its Studios Will Heavily Use AI to Make Future Games
item.dc:creator: Elijah Gonzalez
item.description: Xbox CEO Asha Sharma wrote a post implying the company will lean into using AI to develop its games.
item.content:encoded: This Sunday marks 25 years of Xbox. To commemorate the occasion, Xbox CEO Asha Sharma wrote a lengthy post on X cataloging Microsoft’s long history with gaming that goes back long before the original Xbox was released on Nov. 15, 2001. However, while the post mostly reads like a typical anniversary blog from a gaming executive, the last chunk implies the company may be going in a new direction with the most controversial technology of the moment: generative AI.

item.title: Disney Plus Is Officially the New Streaming Home of the Game Awards
item.dc:creator: Willa Rowe
item.description: Disney Plus has announced it will stream the 2026 Game Awards, hosted by Geoff Keighley
item.content:encoded: In a first for the show, this year's Game Awards will be available to stream on Disney Plus. This is just one additional way to watch the game industry's version of the Oscars, on top of the usual Twitch and YouTube livestreams. The announcement simultaneously expands the offerings on Disney's streaming service and further boosts the awards show's profile.

item.title: Ex-Overwatch 2 Lead: Blizzard Execs Pushing Overwatch 2’s Reveal Were ‘Fucking Idiots’
item.dc:creator: Patricia Hernandez
item.description: The hero shooter's former Game Director Jeff Kaplan dishes on Blizzard's decision to announce Overwatch 2 alongside Diablo 4 back in 2019
item.content:encoded: Former Blizzard game director Jeff Kaplan left the company five years ago, but the studio's Overwatch fumbles are still fresh in his mind, judging by frank remarks he shared during a podcast. In it, the former face of the hero shooter described what was happening behind the scenes leading up to Blizzard's surprise announcement of Overwatch 2. Kaplan said there was deep dysfunction at the executive level within the company.

item.title: Witcher Multiplayer Game Adds Key Writer From Baldur’s Gate 3
item.dc:creator: Willa Rowe
item.description: CD Projekt Red’s multiplayer Witcher game adds Baldur’s Gate 3 writer responsible for Dark Urge and more
item.content:encoded: CD Projekt Red has a lot of irons in the proverbial fire right now, one being a Witcher multiplayer game codenamed Project Sirius. While it was first revealed back in 2022 alongside other projects that would later be confirmed asThe Witcher 4 and a remake of the original Witcher, Sirius has had a troubled development thus far. CD Projekt Red continues to add talent to the project, however, with the latest addition being one of the writers behind some of Baldur's Gate 3's best storylines.

item.title: GTA 6 Map Seemingly Leaks at Merch Drop Event
item.dc:creator: Elijah Gonzalez
item.description: Grand Theft Auto 6's map appears to have leaked early due to a Selfridges event.
item.content:encoded: With Grand Theft Auto 6, Rockstar Games has already experienced some of the highest-profile leaks in gaming history, and it seems at least one more has snuck in before the game’s impending Nov. 19 release. Pictures are circulating of what appears to be a physical poster of GTA 6’s map.

item.title: GTA 6 Nearly Hit With Ban Over ‘Frequent Male Genital Exposure’
item.dc:creator: Jen Glennon
item.description: South Korea's game ratings board took several votes to arrive at an 'Adults Only' rating for GTA 6
item.content:encoded: With the launch of Grand Theft Auto 6 mere days away, we already know to expect a whole lot of mature subject matter. Official promotional materials like the Netflix Extended Look have prominently featured strip clubs, drug deals gone wrong, and chaotic vehicular shootouts. A new report out of South Korea from Inven Global claims members of the Game Content Rating Board (GCRB) nearly refused to issue a rating for GTA 6, which would have effectively banned the game there. The main sticking point? An excessive amount of "out of context genital nudity."

item.title: Are there too many tentacles in Resident Evil?
item.dc:creator: Jake Kleinman
item.description: The VFX wizards at Weta Workshop had their hands full (of tentacles) working on Zach Cregger's Resident Evil.
item.content:encoded: The VFX wizards at Weta Workshop had their hands full (of tentacles) working on Zach Cregger's Resident Evil.

item.title: What We Know About Every Assassin’s Creed Project in Active Development
item.dc:creator: Austin Manchester
item.description: The latest news and release dates for every known Assassin’s Creed project, like Jade and Codename Hexe.
item.content:encoded: Assassin’s Creed will turn 20 years old in 2027. After 15 main series entries and even more handheld and mobile spinoffs, the series is showing no signs of slowing down. Its latest entry was Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced, a remake of 2013’s Assassin’s Creed 4: Black Flag.

item.title: Queen’s Domain Review: The Perfect Skyrim Replacement for Right Now
item.dc:creator: Matt Patches
item.description: Queen's Domain is a brutal first-person Soulslike that borrows all the right things from Dark Souls and Elder Scrolls.
item.content:encoded: I love Skyrim. I love returning to the spine-tingling haze of ’90s first-person games like Doom, Quake, and Myst. But what I really love is a modern game that feels like a lost relic from that era, not a nostalgic imitation but something that might have actually existed.

item.title: New 'GTA 6' Gameplay Leaves Fans Stunned
item.dc:creator: Patricia Hernandez
item.description: GTA 6 fans are doing a double-take on a new gameplay clip shared by Rockstar that almost looks too good to be true
item.content:encoded: With only a week left before the release of Grand Theft Auto 6, there's little in Rockstar Games' marketing that players haven't seen before. That familiarity is true of new GTA 6 features, at least. In terms of visuals, the game developer just proved it still has plenty of Leonida to show off.

item.title: Diablo Meets Hades in New Conan the Barbarian Game
item.dc:creator: Michael McWhertor
item.description: Conan: The Black Pyramid brings Robert E Howard's famous barbarian to life in a new cosmic horror action RPG a la Diablo and Hades.
item.content:encoded: Conan the Barbarian has managed to remain relevant in pop culture for more than 90 years, thanks to literature, film, and video games. In 2028, Conan will return in a new adventure that combines the fantasy franchise's sword-and-sworcery themes with a dash of cosmic horror.

item.title: Blizzard Can't Stop Tweaking WoW: Forever and It's Only Been 6 Days
item.dc:creator: Oli Welsh
item.description: Hotfix changes for World of Warcraft: Forever on Nov. 10 included class balance, quest gold rewards, and more
item.content:encoded: While Blizzard has vowed to issue a major balance patch for World of Warcraft: Foreverwhen the retro MMO's raids launch in December, the developer certainly doesn't seem afraid of doing some tinkering under the hood in the meantime. A roundup of hotfixes published on Nov. 10 would put the full patch notes of many live-service games to shame. And we're just six days out from launch.

item.title: Lord of the Rings: The Hunt for Gollum Officially Wraps Filming
item.dc:creator: Willa Rowe
item.category: The Lord of the Rings: The Hunt for Gollum
item.description: Lord of the Rings: The Hunt for Gollum director Andy Serkis confirms principal photography has finished ahead of its 2027 release.
item.content:encoded: We are one step closer to seeing a new Lord of the Rings film in theaters. Andy Serkis has confirmed that principal photography on The Hunt for Gollum has been completed, which he is directing in addition to reprising the titular role that made him famous. The movie is currently slated to be released on Dec. 17, 2027.

item.title: My Grandma Got Me Through the Water Temple. She Would’ve Loved the Ocarina of Time Remake
item.dc:creator: Corey Plante
item.category: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time
The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time
item.description: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake brings back memories of playing the Nintendo 64 original with my grandma.
item.content:encoded: For a while it was the NES. I’d shoot ducks until I got bored, and I hated Mario because it was too hard. What I really remember fondly was watching Mémère play The Legend of Zelda: A Link to the Past after she upgraded to the SNES. She’d tell me who she was fighting and why, and following along felt like having one of my favorite people read me a book. When it was my turn to play, I’d just charge up Link’s sword and mow every blade of grass I could find. Then I’d go looking for chickens. Then I’d ask what she had for snacks. She always had good snacks for me.

item.title: Tom Morello Joins Critical Role for New Bard-Themed Adventure
item.dc:creator: Aimee Hart
item.description: A new Critical Role charity one-shot featuring Rage Against the Machine's Tom Morello, with Matthew Mercer as Game Master, is scheduled for Nov. 17.
item.content:encoded: The founders of Critical Role have always taken pride in shaking up the way they play tabletop role-playing games. But next week, a new adventure will push the cast and crew further than ever: a "Battle of the Bards," with Matthew Mercer as Game Master.

item.title: Dragon Quest Creator Says New Game Will Capture the Series' 'Unmistakable Feeling'
item.dc:creator: Ashely Claudino
item.description: A turn-based Dragon Quest RPG is set to launch on smartphones next year, allowing fans to enjoy a classic adventure anywhere they go.
item.content:encoded: The Dragon Quest series has taken players on countless journeys over the past four decades. Next year, fans will be able to embark on a new Dragon Quest adventure using their smartphones with the launch of Dragon Quest RPG The Cursed Tree and The Chosen Isle.

item.title: Magic's Best Unofficial Format Is So Big, Burger King Is Running a Tournament
item.dc:creator: Francesco Cacciatore
item.description: Burger Kind and Magic: The Gathering are collaborating in Italy with an exclusive deck box and sleeves, plus a Pauper tournament series.
item.content:encoded: If you think that the Universe Beyond crossover with beloved sci-fi franchise Star Trek is the biggest thing currently going on in the Magic: The Gathering world, think again. On Nov. 10, details emerged from Italy about a country-exclusive collaboration between Magic and fast-food chain Burger King. Fans and players worldwide are going wild online about the Burger King-themed sleeves and deck box, but there is more to this unexpected campaign.
